title: Infrastructure weekly update - 2026-05-11
content:
Highlights:

- APAC (ap-southeast-1) pilot region is now serving production traffic for two internal customers (canary wave 1). Median 95th-percentile tail latency improved from ~210ms to ~160ms for short chat requests relative to routing through us-west.
- Fleet utilization stabilized after last week's demand spike: cluster-wide GPU utilization at 62% (down from 78% peak on 2026-05-04). Booking/allocations aligned with current committed capacity.
- Autoscaling policy tuning rolled out: reduced scale-up aggressiveness for memory-heavy workloads and increased prewarm pool for low-latency routes - saw ~12% fewer cold starts in staging.

Capacity and procurement:

- Immediate need: 40 additional A100-80G-equivalent GPUs to meet projected Dedicated customer ramp in Q3 (estimate: +25% peak throughput).
  - Procurement request submitted to finance on 2026-05-09 (CloudTicket:AWS-REQ-99872). Approvals pending.
- Short-term plan: reallocate 8 reserved GPUs from lower-utilized EU test pool to US production to cover next 3 weeks of overcommit. Ops will perform the reallocation on 2026-05-13 during the 02:00-04:00 UTC maintenance window.
- Long-term: evaluating spot-resistant packing + mixed-instance families to reduce unit cost. Next step: run a 2-week pricing simulation with mixed-family placements (A100 + H100) starting 2026-05-18.

Regional updates:

- us-west-2: Stable. No incidents. Average GPU utilization 66%. Disk I/O hotspots observed on node group infra-gpu-w2-3 - IO coordinator patch merged (PR #412) to reduce checkpoint burst writes.
- eu-west-1: Elevated utilization on dedicated pools (78%), prioritized traffic remains within SLA. Monitoring threshold raised to trigger advance scaling at 82%.
- ap-southeast-1: Pilot live for canary customers. Observed improved latency for APAC users (p95 down from ~210ms to ~160ms). Identified two lower-priority models that exhibit memory growth after ~120 minutes - created follow-up ticket (INFRA-2398).

Incidents and reliability:

- 2026-05-07 (sev-2): transient control-plane throttling caused ~15 minutes of elevated scheduling latency for the long-tail queue. Root cause: retry storm from legacy job resubmitter. Mitigation: rate limit applied and resubmitter disabled; full fix in PR #412. No customer-facing outages.
- Checkpoint corruption observed on one eu-west-1 node during large-model snapshot (2026-05-10). Corruption contained to ephemeral storage; snapshot integrity checks prevented promotion. Action: add checksum verification to snapshot pipeline (owner: Priya, due 2026-05-18).

Autoscaling and runtime optimizations:

- Batching threshold adjustment released to staging: target batch size reduces by 10% for conversational routes to improve latency at the 95th percentile. Early results: p95 latency improved ~8% with ~3% throughput loss.
- KV-cache TTL decreased from 6h to 2h for aggressive multi-tenant pools to free GPU RAM for hot models; continues to be monitored.
- Quantization profile rollout: half of the candidate models moved to 4-bit inference in staging; no quality regressions observed on the evaluation suite. Plan to expand to canary customers next week.

Cost and packing:

- Packing improvements from last sprint reduced per-token GPU cost by ~6% for baseline workloads. We will continue to iterate on allocation heuristics (PR cadence weekly).
- Proposal to increase burst-capacity budget by 18% during product launch windows (justification attached in Confluence). Finance review scheduled for 2026-05-15.

Action items and owners:

- Alex Chen: Follow up with finance on AWS-REQ-99872 procurement approval (due 2026-05-14).
- Priya Patel: Implement snapshot checksum and add automated recovery test (INFRA-2398) (due 2026-05-18).
- Riley Martinez: Execute reallocation of 8 GPUs from EU test cluster to US production (maintenance window 2026-05-13).
- Evan Brooks: Run 2-week mixed-instance pricing simulation (start 2026-05-18) and share results in next update.
- Jordan Kim: Increase staging canary cohort for 4-bit quantized models and collect quality metrics (due 2026-05-20).

Risks and blockers:

- Procurement latency from cloud provider and internal finance approval may delay Dedicated customer commitments. Contingency: temporary burst credits and prioritized preemption policy.
- KMS/HSM integration for Private deployments remains a blocker for one near-term regulated customer - waiting on security sign-off for the proposed HSM design (security review scheduled 2026-05-19).

Notes / Context / References:

- See runbook for stress testing GPU pools: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/GPU+Fleet+Runbook
- Related Jira: INFRA-2345 (autoscaling tuning), INFRA-2398 (snapshot integrity).
- Infra PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/412 (IO coordinator patch).

Next week focus:

- Secure procurement approvals or finalize temporary burst plan.
- Finish snapshot integrity fix and add E2E recovery test.
- Expand APAC canary to three additional customers and monitor behavior under realistic traffic.
- Begin mixed-instance cost simulation and present preliminary numbers in next weekly update.

If you want deeper details on any section above - ping me or add items to the weekly infra sync agenda.
